sources.articleTitle: Another ‘encounter’ in West Bengal: Rape-murder accused killed in Raiganj
CM Suvendu defends encounter in Raiganj, says police entitled to retaliate in self-defence
Rape-murder accused gunned down in Bengal; 4th encounter since BJP came to power

headline: West Bengal Police Kill Rape-Murder Suspect In Raiganj Encounter
seoTitle: Rape-Murder Suspect Killed In West Bengal Police Encounter
metaDescription: A suspect accused of murdering his niece was killed by police in Raiganj, marking the fourth such fatal encounter since the BJP took power in the state.
aiSummaryBullets: A man accused of raping and murdering his young niece was killed during a police operation in Raiganj, West Bengal.
Police reported the suspect initiated gunfire, leading officers to retaliate in what they described as an act of self-defense.
This incident represents the fourth fatal police encounter recorded in West Bengal since the BJP assumed state government leadership.
aiContextParagraph: The incident in Raiganj follows a series of lethal police confrontations in West Bengal involving criminal suspects. Following the death of the accused, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari defended the actions of the law enforcement team, stating that officers retain the right to use force in self-defense during arrests. The deceased individual was under investigation for the rape and murder of his young niece. According to official reports, this event marks the fourth instance of a suspect being killed by police since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) administration took office in May. Previous encounters occurred in regions including Gaighata, Baruipur, and Dhulian, involving individuals suspected of rape and murder. The latest development has drawn attention to the state government's approach to policing and criminal apprehension, as authorities maintain that the actions taken by responding units were necessary responses to direct threats.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained traction due to reports from multiple news outlets detailing a pattern of fatal police encounters under the new state government.
